verdict.rationale: LiteLLM's self-hosted proxy issues virtual keys that it manages itself. Those keys can control model access and track spend. Keys can be team-scoped (the docs contrast team keys with ones created 'without team_id'), and the gateway puts the whole AI stack 'behind one key', which implies provider credentials stay on the gateway. One community comment mentions vague trouble creating tokens for other users; it is not a concrete counter-example, so it lowers confidence only. Missing for 10: an explicit statement that raw provider keys are never exposed to key holders, detailed key-generation API or UI documentation for team and app keys, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a platform engineer, I can mint gateway-managed keys for teams and apps without exposing raw provider keys

citations.quote: Self-hosted LLM Gateway (Proxy) with virtual keys, cost tracking, and an admin UI
Track Spend, and control model access via virtual keys for the proxy
Create virtual keys without team_id for individual spending limits
Put your full AI stack behind one key.
Track spend for keys, users, and teams across 100+ LLMs.
